summary: O-025: OutcomePanel and SL-039's TopLevelPanel are now the two rows of one Grid, which is the window's last child. A row is star-sized only while its panel is visible. During a scan the results list gets all the space; after an ending the two split it 2:1. The outcome row never drops below 316 px, or 328 px while the unreadable list is open. The two outcome lists' MinHeight is now 24 px (one row), down from 40, so in tight space they shrink and keep scrolling instead of being clipped. O-026: the report gained additive TopLevelPanel {visible, actualHeight} and TopLevelList {actualHeight, inView, realizedRows} keys. New case B-007 fills the largest-files list across 36 top-level folders and asserts at 880x600 that LargestFilesList and TopLevelList are both in view after a Completed and after a Cancelled ending, each with the unreadable list closed and opened. It also checks that mid-scan the results list is taller than after the ending. For the Cancelled-and-opened run, the hook's watch mode accepts FSA_HOOK_EXPAND=1. B-007 fails on the attempt-4 layout with TopLevelList at 0 px, and every non-network window case, the hook cases, Core.Tests and the rules checks pass on the final tree. On the real system drive at 880x600 all lists are in view both closed and opened, but opened the outcome's lists get only 28–30 px each and the results list 19 px.

files.why: O-025. OutcomePanel and TopLevelPanel now sit in one Grid, the last child of the outer DockPanel. Row 0 (outcome) is Auto while collapsed and 2* while visible, with MinHeight 316, or 328 while UnreadableExpander is open and visible. Row 1 (results) is Auto while collapsed and 1* while visible. OutcomePanel loses DockPanel.Dock and gains VerticalAlignment=Top, so an ending with no list stays as tall as its texts. LargestFilesList and UnreadableList MinHeight go from 40 to 24. The TopLevelPanel comment is rewritten and a comment explains the new Grid. The two panels are re-indented inside the Grid (whitespace only).

O-026. Adds window.TopLevelPanel {visible, actualHeight} and window.TopLevelList {actualHeight, inView, realizedRows}, additive under schema 1 per the x:Name convention, and documents them in the schema comment.

Watch mode accepts FSA_HOOK_EXPAND=1. It registers expand's watcher before the window loads, so a Cancel's ending also opens the unreadable list (logged as 'acted mode=expand'). Any other value, or the variable with any other mode, is refused. The watch line gains listHeight=px, the results list's height as Cancel is pressed. The header docs are updated.

Adds the CheckBothLists helper and case B-007: 4 folders of 26 non-empty files, 12 list-denied folders and 20 slow folders of 1,500 empty folders each, run as Completed closed, Completed opened (expand), Cancelled closed (watch) and Cancelled opened (watch with FSA_HOOK_EXPAND=1). B-003 now also asserts TopLevelList inView when closed and opened. Read-WatchLine parses listHeight. FSA_HOOK_EXPAND is added to $HookVariables, and B-007 to the ValidateSet, $HookedCases, the All list and the header.

The window section no longer says TopLevelPanel is the window's last child and gets the rest of the height. It now describes the shared Grid: all the space during a scan; 2:1 with the outcome floors after an ending; header and part of a row at 880x600.

obligations.how: In MainWindow.xaml, OutcomePanel and TopLevelPanel now share one star-row Grid that takes the rest of the window's height. Each row collapses to Auto (0 px) while its panel is collapsed, so during a scan the results list has all the height (167.5 px mid-scan, from the hook's watch line). After an ending the split is 2:1 with an outcome floor of 316 px, or 328 px while the unreadable list is open. Re-running B-003 at 880x600: closed gives TopLevelList 31.3 px in view; opened gives LargestFilesList 60.6 px, UnreadableList 51.3 px and TopLevelList 19.3 px, all in view, so O-024's split still holds. On the real system drive (C:\, 3,584,794 files, 663 unreadable) at 880x600: closed gives LargestFilesList 46.1 px, UnreadableExpander and TopLevelList 31.3 px, all in view; opened gives LargestFilesList 28.3 px, UnreadableList 29.8 px and TopLevelList 19.3 px, all in view. The attempt-4 layout gave TopLevelPanel 0 px. The TopLevelPanel comment and docs/design/SL-039-live-results.md are updated.

The report now carries TopLevelPanel {visible, actualHeight} and TopLevelList {actualHeight, inView, realizedRows}, additive under schema 1. New case B-007 (104 non-empty files, 36 top-level folders, 12 unreadable) asserts at 880x600 that LargestFilesList and TopLevelList are both inView after Completed, closed and opened with expand mode. It asserts the same after Cancel (watch mode), closed and opened (watch with FSA_HOOK_EXPAND=1), and checks that the mid-scan list is taller than after the stop. It passes. Against the attempt-4 layout, all four runs fail with TopLevelList 0 px not in view.

deviations: The split is 2:1 with an outcome floor, not the equal stars the B1 disposition gave as an example. Measured at 880x600, 385 px is left for both panels. Keeping the largest-files list in view needs about 256 px of outcome (Completed, closed), 300 px (Completed, opened), 321 px (Cancelled, opened, whose title wraps) and 309 px (system drive, closed). Equal stars give the outcome 193 px, which fails even the closed case. A plain 3:1 star split, measured, failed both opened runs. So the outcome row is 2* with MinHeight 316, or 328 while the unreadable list is open. That leaves the results list its header and 19–31 px of list at the default size. Windows taller than about 710 px share by the stars alone.

LargestFilesList and UnreadableList MinHeight went from 40 to 24 px (one row). With 40, the system drive opened at 880x600 clipped both outcome lists by about 12 px: they were drawn at 40 px in about 28 px of room, measured as not in view. With 24 they shrink to 28.3 and 29.8 px and stay whole and scrollable. On the planted trees they are unchanged and still at least 40 px (B-003's two-row checks still pass).

OutcomePanel is now VerticalAlignment=Top in its star row. An ending with no list (Could not read, Scan failed) stays as tall as its texts, as uat's top-docked panel did, instead of stretching a coloured box over the row.

To reach the Cancelled-and-opened shape the disposition asked for, the hook got FSA_HOOK_EXPAND=1, accepted with watch mode only. The watch line also gained listHeight for the live-scan check. Both are additive; every SL-039 case (L-001 to L-003, M-001) and HookCases still pass.
follow_ups: What window size must hold all three lists? At the default 880x600, after an ending the results list gets only its header and 19–31 px of list, and on the system drive with the unreadable folders open the outcome's lists get 28–30 px each. Below the default (the window allows 560x400) the outcome's floor pushes the results list off the bottom. A larger default window, a higher MinHeight, tabs or a side-by-side layout is a design-slice choice across SL-039 and SL-040. The reflect already lists the question.

The report's layout keys depend on whether the drive buttons have loaded before a fast scan ends. LoadDrives is awaited after StartScan, so a sub-second scan can end with an empty DrivePanel and about 54 px more room: B-003 read TopLevelList at 85.2 px once and 31.3 px otherwise. Layout assertions should hold in the tighter case (they do now), or the report should wait for the drives.

tests.note: A step while choosing the split. Opened: LargestFilesList and UnreadableList at 40 px were not in view with OutcomePanel at 272.9 px. That measurement is why the outcome floors exist.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case B-007 (plain 3:1 star split, before the floors)
tests.note: Closed runs passed. Both opened runs, Completed and Cancelled, failed with LargestFilesList not in view. The watch cancel did land mid-scan with 100 rows, 12 unreadable and 15–17 folders not read.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case B-007 (against HEAD's attempt-4 MainWindow.xaml, as a mutant; file restored and hash-checked)
tests.note: Failed as intended. All four endings reported TopLevelList 0 px, not in view, while LargestFilesList was 82–169 px, so B-007 detects B1.

Final tree, exe republished at the start: 25 passed (C-001 to C-014, O-016, L-001 to L-003, B-001 to B-007). N-001 to N-004 were not run: they change SMB mappings. B-007 at 880x600: Completed closed gives LargestFilesList 99.96 and TopLevelList 31.26 px; Completed opened gives 60.6 / UnreadableList 51.3 / TopLevelList 19.3; Cancelled closed gives 78.7 / 31.3; Cancelled opened gives 47.9 / 42.8 / 19.3. All in view. Mid-scan list height is 167.5 px.
H-001 and H-002 pass with the changed hook.

tests.command: eng/read-window.ps1 -Root C:\ (system drive, 880x600, list closed; throwaway script in %TEMP%, since deleted)
tests.note: Real entry point, published exe with MinHeight 40. Completed: 3,584,780 files, 211 s, largestFilesMs 29.2. OutcomePanel 300, LargestFilesList 46.1 px in view, UnreadableExpander in view, TopLevelList 31.3 px in view, topLevel.rows 37. A first attempt read a stale mutant exe (Copy-Item had kept the old mtime, so nothing republished) and was discarded; the file was touched and the exe republished.
663 unreadable, opened. LargestFilesList and UnreadableList were not in view: 40 px each in about 28 px of room. TopLevelList was 19.3 px and in view. This is why the lists' MinHeight went to 24.

3,584,794 files, 206 s, largestFilesMs 37.8. OutcomePanel 312, LargestFilesList 28.3 px, UnreadableExpander, UnreadableList 29.8 px and TopLevelList 19.3 px, all in view. The only XAML change after this run was a comment.
